projects.title: AI Society Corpus
projects.summary: An interactive knowledge graph that turns NUS AI Society's AI/ML learning material into connected study paths rather than isolated pages.
projects.problem: AI/ML learners need to see how concepts depend on, resemble, and refer to one another—not merely read a long list of topics.
projects.method: Topics live in validated Markdown with structured frontmatter. A static Astro build derives prerequisite, tag-similarity, and WikiLink-backlink edges, then renders them through React and a D3 force graph.
projects.result: The corpus gives readers a navigable concept network alongside a reviewable contribution workflow, content validation, unit tests, and Playwright checks.

projects.title: Beryl
projects.summary: A repository-owned guarantee layer for AI-assisted development: it makes workflow rules, checks, and review boundaries visible before agent output is trusted.
projects.problem: Scattered prompts and instruction files can guide an agent, but they do not provide one source of truth or evidence that repository rules were followed.
projects.method: Beryl installs a durable control plane for task routing, project context, deterministic checks, test-manifest protection, and optional local Git hooks—while preserving human review.
projects.result: Teams get a repeatable loop of intent, bounded changes, checks, evidence, and signoff that is inspectable in the repository instead of trapped in chat history.

projects.title: Notes — this site
projects.summary: The site you are reading: a static technical-notes system that turns a personal study corpus into searchable, shareable, reliable public work.
projects.problem: Technical notes lose value when source structure, mathematical notation, code, navigation, and discovery break as they move from a private workspace to the web.
projects.method: A strict Notion ingestion pipeline normalizes topic trees at build time; separate rendering and styling boundaries publish static Cloudflare Pages routes, search, metadata, RSS, and portfolio evidence.
projects.result: The site preserves nested note paths, LaTeX, code blocks, and source formatting while producing a fast static archive with deterministic build checks.

projects.title: SIAP
projects.summary: Structure and Interpretation of Agentic Patterns: a theory-backed, publishable book for making agent orchestration more explicit, testable, and teachable.
projects.problem: Agent engineering is often held together by framework defaults, prompt folklore, and local craft knowledge, leaving objectives, memory, tool contracts, and failure modes under-specified.
projects.method: The manuscript teaches agent systems by construction: Markdown chapters connect decision theory, planning, retrieval, safety, and multi-agent coordination to interpreters for reasoning and tool-use loops. Python scripts produce a static reader and print-ready artifacts.
projects.result: SIAP publishes a navigable, MathJax-enabled web book and PDF outputs, with citation rules, editorial audits, and reproducible manuscript checks protecting the research program.
